synopsis: Re-verified from the retained bytes: all 39 artifacts hash-match their addresses, all 26 SHA256SUMS entries resolve to hash-correct blobs, 116/116 gold and OCR reproduce from the raw BIO tags, the documented split procedure reproduces the manifest IDs exactly, and the stdlib evaluator passes 9/9 hand-checked cases plus my own fixtures. All four criteria hold.
notes: Independently verified against the pinned artifacts (no producer notes relied on). Method: read the Merv blob store directly; (1) recomputed sha256 of all 39 blobs - every one equals its content-addressed filename, and the 26 SHA256SUMS entries each map to a blob whose bytes hash to the listed value; (2) parsed the retained rows-API pages myself and re-implemented BIO span decoding from the info.json tag names, reproducing the OCR words, tag digits and all four gold strings of all 116 kit records (0 mismatches) plus the full 973-row source statistics; (3) re-implemented the documented group-shuffle-quota selection with seed 20260918 and got exactly the same demonstration/development/holdout receipt-id sets as splits_manifest.json; (4) recomputed the dataset canonical hash (804d5937...), the file plain sha256, all three per-split hashes and both freeze hashes - all match; (5) concatenated the delivered parquet chunks and confirmed both reassembled PAR1 files match the pinned parquet sha256 and the work tree; (6) ran the shipped evaluate.py and selftest_evaluator.py on the frozen data (9/9 fixtures, perfect demo 1.0000, perfect holdout 1.0000, corrupted demo overall 0.4792 / whole 0.4167 / invalid 0.5000 with the six cited reasons and 1 ignored unknown id) and additionally scored my own hand-computed fixtures for perfect/wrong/missing/malformed/non-object/non-string/extra/duplicate/unknown-id/unparseable input, whose hand-derived expectations (e.g. 7/16 fields, 0.25 whole) the evaluator reproduced exactly; (7) validated the exclusion ledger against the raw rows (15 duplicate rows with correct normalized-text sha256 pointing at a kept row with identical text, plus train row 104 X51005663280 genuinely lacking an ADDRESS span in the tags), confirmed 958 distinct normalized OCR texts and 372 company groups over all 973 rows, and confirmed the visibility rule (only demonstration_split.json / demonstration_receipts.txt are label-displayable; no dev/holdout id appears in the demo text). Non-blocking observations, none affecting the criteria: (a) observed_check_outputs.txt section G lists kit_manifests.tar.gz as 12701 bytes and kit_evidence.tar.gz as 25030 bytes, which are earlier within-session pack sizes - the delivered archives are 13055 and 25265 bytes (the log was written before the final repack, and it already defers hashes to SHA256SUMS); I re-verified that the delivered archive members are byte-identical to the checked working tree, so the recorded 27/27 and 9/9 results still describe the delivered bytes; (b) README says "all 14 retained rows-API response bodies" while the manifest lists 16 endpoints (11 rows pages + 5 metadata); (c) evaluate.py's docstring documents that a malformed prediction entry invalidates the whole predictions file, but the README invalid-output list does not mention that path. None of these is a false claim about the data, the splits, or the scoring.

I recomputed sha256 for all 17 retained payload files and every one matches the manifest (0 mismatches), so the hashes are real pins. Schema/tag mapping is read from the retained info.json, whose ClassLabel names are exactly [O, B-COMPANY, I-COMPANY, B-DATE, I-DATE, B-ADDRESS, I-ADDRESS, B-TOTAL, I-TOTAL] with tag_index_mapping 0..8; I read that file directly and confirm the mapping was inspected, not guessed. Available counts verified: 973 rows = train 626 + test 347 with max row_idx 625/346, 958 distinct normalized OCR texts and 372 distinct normalized company groups over all 973 rows - I recomputed both counts and got the same numbers. Licensing is handled as fact plus uncertainty: the mirror's info.json license is the empty string with no licence file in the repo (I confirmed license='' and repo files sroie.py/.gitattributes), ICDAR-2019 SROIE provenance and the MIT-licensed secondary key repo are recorded, and the manifest explicitly states the redistribution licence status is UNKNOWN. All 16 exclusions are enumerated with reasons and evidence. Retention is real: the 9 rows-API archives hold every response body plus fetch_manifest.json, and the two parquet files are retained as 6 raw chunks that I concatenated and confirmed hash to the pinned d8e3afe4.../07df54d3... PAR1 files.

I re-derived the dataset from the retained source payloads with my own BIO decoder. For all 116 records the newline-encoded OCR words are verbatim from the raw pages, the tag digits match exactly, and all four reconstructed gold strings match exactly (116/116, zero mismatches) - gold is genuinely reconstructed from the documented tags and no row is synthesised. Stable ids follow sroie-hf-<source split>-<canonical filename stem> (regex confirmed on all 116) and each maps to a distinct (source_split, source_row_index). splits_manifest.json records seed 20260918, targets and exact counts 12/24/80, all split ids, the full selection procedure, the visibility rule and interpretation limits. Hashes verified: canonical record hash 804d59370b... equals the manifest, the file plain sha256 3abff953... matches, all three per-split hashes match, and holdout_freeze.json's dataset/development/holdout hashes all match my recomputation. Leakage checks pass on my own counts: 0 duplicate normalized OCR texts anywhere in the kit and 0 normalized-company overlap across splits (70 groups among the 116 selected records). Rerunnability is proven rather than asserted: I re-implemented the documented procedure from the manifest text (global OCR dedup keeping the first (split,row_idx) row, grouping by normalize_text(company), sorted keys shuffled with random.Random(20260918), greedy quota assignment with deterministic repair) and reproduced exactly the manifest's demonstration, development and holdout id sets, with remaining quotas closing at 0. The visibility rule also holds: demonstration_split.json is byte-identical to the demonstration subset of the dataset, demonstration_receipts.txt contains exactly the 12 demonstration ids, and no development/holdout id appears in it.

evaluate.py imports only argparse, json, os, re, sys and unicodedata - standard library only, confirmed from the shipped source, whose archive members I checked are byte-identical to the bytes I ran. Normalization is documented in both the script and the README as NFKC + casefold + whitespace-collapse + strip, with matching by exact equality and no punctuation/currency/numeric folding; I confirmed behaviorally that RM 9.00 != 9.00 and that case/NFKC/whitespace variants do match. Reported quantities are per-field accuracy for company/date/address/total, overall field accuracy (correct cells / 4N), whole-receipt exact accuracy and invalid-output rate; no F1 is reported. The shipped selftest passes 9/9, and I independently hand-checked those expectations (missing-field case 4/12 overall, 2/3 invalid, 1/3 per field; extra field 0.5; duplicate 0.5; currency case 0.75 overall / 0.0 whole). Beyond the shipped fixtures I scored my own cases and they matched my own hand-derived numbers: valid-but-wrong values are not invalid (0.4375 overall, 0.25 whole, 0.5 invalid for one wrong-field row plus one extra-field row and one absent row); malformed JSON, non-object JSON, non-string raw, non-string field value, missing prediction, duplicate entry, unknown receipt id, non-dict entry, list-valued payload and a None payload are each flagged with the correct reason; unknown ids are reported and ignored. Missing/extra/non-string are handled explicitly (exactly four required string keys, extras rejected).

The delivery links a complete immutable kit. Every one of the 26 SHA256SUMS entries resolves to a blob whose recomputed sha256 equals the listed value (26/26), and all 26 archive members of the four kit archives are byte-identical to the working tree the checks ran against. Commands are independently reproducible: fetch_source.py/fetch_key.py re-fetch from the pinned public URLs and revisions with stdlib urllib, build_kit.py regenerates the dataset deterministically (I reproduced its selection output independently), and the README gives exact extraction and shasum -c commands; the parquet chunks reassemble to the pinned hashes. Observed check outputs are recorded (verify_kit 27/27, selftest 9/9, perfect demonstration and holdout 1.0000, corrupted demonstration 0.4792/0.4167/0.5000). I could not execute verify_kit.py here because the filesystem is read-only and it rebuilds into a work directory, so I instead independently reproduced every one of its 27 assertions (payload hashes, 973 rows, counts 12/24/80, per-split hashes, unique and pattern-valid ids, distinct source rows, lossless newline encoding, digit-only tags, gold non-empty and recomputable, no duplicate text, no company overlap, exclusion ledger shape, duplicate pointers, source accounting, freeze contents and hashes, demo artifact identity, and verbatim coverage of every excluded row). Limitations are stated honestly: gold is reconstructed from BIO spans rather than canonical target JSON with measured agreement (date 610/626, total 562/626, company 492/626, address 356/626) that I recomputed exactly from the canonical-key payloads, address is called the weakest field, company grouping is explicitly a heuristic that does not guarantee corporate-family independence, the 116-receipt Malay/English benchmark is small with wide intervals, the mirror declares no licence, and the mirror builder's 455 MB original zip was not downloaded.

synopsis: Reproduced the frozen prompts P0/P1/P2 byte-exactly from the delivered kit under the plan's own rules; confirmed 12/24/80 splits, 44 holdout company groups (largest 15), zero company overlap, demonstration-only candidate material. Controls, metric, cluster-aware uncertainty and pre-registered decision rules are defensible; power limits and the P2 confound are disclosed.
notes: Reviewed only the pinned submission (plan.md, sha256 6885f227...). I recomputed rather than trusting prose, using the retained kit blobs and the frozen plan text. Pass on all three criteria. Verification performed: (1) frozen prompts reconstruct byte-for-byte under the plan's stated conventions - P0 = P0_TASK+"\n\n"+OUTPUT_FORMAT is 519 chars with sha256 3de152a6...; P1 is 1674 chars with 06ebd802...; P2 is 2602 chars with fc04c0cd... (P2 matches only when the three shortest demonstration receipts are enumerated in the plan's listed id order, which the plan does specify), so the hypothesis is stated against fixed, reconstructible strings; (2) kit facts the design depends on are true - 116 records in 12/24/80 splits, 116 distinct flat OCR texts, zero normalized-company overlap across all three split pairs, 80 holdout receipts in 44 company groups with a largest group of 15 (so the dominant-cluster sensitivity is meaningful); (3) leakage is structurally prevented - every distinctive P1 example ("STAR GROCER SDN BHD", "PANA JAYA ENTERPRISE", "(1171881-W)", "25/03/18", "01-02-2018", "10-05-2017", "Rounded Total (RM)", "TAXABLE AMT") occurs in demonstration receipts, no development/holdout company string appears in any prompt, and P2 contains only demonstration OCR text plus demonstration gold. Non-blocking observations, none affecting a criterion: (a) the plan's drafting check says no dev/holdout gold string appears in the prompts "except 27/06/18", but demonstration-derived numerals 5.90, 50.00 and 9.90 also coincide with development/holdout totals; they enter only from demonstration material by construction, so this is an inaccurate self-check sentence, not label leakage; (b) the FIELD_RULES trailing-newline convention is not stated explicitly and is pinned only by the hash assertion; (c) which receipts the <=6 smoke calls use is unspecified; (d) with 80 receipts and a gate requiring both receipt-level and cluster-level interval lows above zero, a true 3-point effect will often fall into the pre-registered "directional only, not confirmed" class - the design accepts this and still produces a bounded, honest answer.

findings.notes: H1 is a specific, falsifiable claim (delta >= 0.03 on 80 frozen holdout receipts) with five pre-registered outcome classes applied once by code, so support, directional-only, sub-threshold and null results are distinguished from each other. Alternatives are addressed explicitly: error attribution (model_miss / unsupported_gold / format / near_miss) separates genuine model errors from BIO-reconstruction label artifacts (address canonical agreement ~57%), and the plan states that a P2 gain confounds content with prompt length and that one prompt instance per arm cannot support a procedure-general claim. I verified the hypothesis is stated against fixed strings: all three frozen prompts reproduce byte-exactly from the delivered kit under the plan's own assembly rules (P0 519 chars / 3de152a6..., P1 1674 / 06ebd802..., P2 2602 / fc04c0cd...).

P0 is a matched control rather than a straw man: the shared output-format paragraph is byte-identical across arms and the user message is byte-identical per receipt, so the P1-vs-P0 contrast isolates extraction guidance from format compliance, and the holdout comparison is paired because both arms score the same 80 receipts. Data are the frozen kit, which I re-checked independently: counts 12/24/80, 116 distinct flat OCR texts, zero normalized-company overlap across every split pair, 44 holdout company groups with a largest group of 15. Candidate material is provably demonstration-only. The primary metric is the claim's own normalized-exact field accuracy, the analysis unit is the receipt rather than the field, and selection/tie, invalidation and decision rules are all fixed before any call with a pre-holdout checkpoint. A minor reporting inaccuracy noted in my top-level notes (the drafting check misses three demonstration-derived numeral collisions) does not reflect leakage or weaken the comparison.

Budget and mechanics match the stated broker constraints: 72 development + 160 holdout = 232 scored calls plus <=6 smoke calls, against a 400-attempt ceiling, <=4 concurrent, transient retries capped at two with backoff and every attempt logged. Failure handling is explicit and honest - a receipt with no successful call stays in the denominator and scores invalid, with a complete-pairs sensitivity alongside. Nine pre-registered invalidation conditions (dataset/evaluator drift, prompt drift, contamination, post-score prompt edits, settings drift, budget/concurrency breaches, >10% unscored holdout, >10-point invalid-rate gap, missing predictions or checkpoint) make non-confirmation auditable rather than negotiable. Limitations are openly stated: one sample per cell so sampling variance is unmeasured, a noisy 24-receipt selection stage, the P2 content/length confound, heuristic company clustering, and BIO-derived gold. The main residual risk is that the cluster-robust gate makes a true 3-point effect likely to land as directional-only, but the plan pre-registers that outcome and the task accepts an uncertainty-bounded pilot.

synopsis: All scored metrics, both bootstrap intervals, token means and the error audit reproduce exactly from the pinned evidence, and the not-confirmed verdict is honest and well supported. But the report cites superseded bundle and exhibit hashes, and the proposed paper text claims all 237 attempts are in the run logs while one smoke attempt is absent.
notes: I independently reconstructed every pinned artifact in memory (revision C bundle = sha256 798c00e0..., 23 payload files verified against its internal SHA256SUMS; superseded revision B = 0864e1f6...), unpacked the inherited kit and the operator journal (237 exact requests, gzip sha256 72757dc6..., raw sha256 c1c09ecd...), and recomputed the science with the frozen kit evaluator (sha256 7980231e...) against the kit dataset (sha256 3abff953...). Every measurement reproduces: dev P0/P1/P2 0.7396/0.8333/0.8438; holdout P0 0.8250 (264/320), P2 0.8719 (279/320); delta +0.046875; receipt bootstrap [0.009375, 0.084375] and company-cluster bootstrap [-0.003425, 0.089744] both reproduce with random.Random(20260918); dominant-cluster sensitivity 0.034615; all 80 per-receipt cell counts match; error audit 39 model_miss/2 near_miss/0 unsupported_gold verified against gold-in-input. Timing, concurrency (max 4), 237 attempts, zero retries/failures, frozen prompts (P0 3de152a6..., P1 06ebd802..., P2 fc04c0cd...) and freeze-before-holdout ordering all check out, with candidate material drawn only from demonstration-split rows. The failures are reporting-fidelity, not scientific: the report describes a superseded evidence pack, and one retained paper sentence is not supported by the logs. Both are cheap to fix.

Submitted measurements agree with the retained results. Numbers in the proposed paper edits verify (0.8250/0.8719, +0.0469, [0.0094,0.0844], [-0.0034,0.0897], 39 model_miss/2 near_miss/0 unsupported_gold, 486->1343 tokens, 2.76x), but one methods sentence is not supported by the retained evidence. It states 'every attempt, retry, HTTP status, UTC timestamp, broker receipt, token count, raw response and parse result is retained in the run logs'; the run logs contain only 236 of the 237 broker attempts. run_log_smoke.jsonl holds 4 rows (broker numbers 2-5), while the first smoke attempt (broker number 1, 02:43:49.590Z, P0 on sroie-hf-test-X51006008166) appears only in the operator journal (art_18d638429e994c29ae7542d31cdbbb63), not in any producer run log. Required correction: add that attempt's row to run_log_smoke.jsonl (or attach the journal row) and either keep the sentence with a one-line disclosure of the extra operator-retained smoke call, or narrow it to 'all scored attempts are logged'. While revising, also update the report's bundle hash to revision C (798c00e0...) / 23 payload files and its exhibit hash (598c078a...).

Three non-blocking prose/metadata residuals are recorded for a later tidy-up.

synopsis: Independently reassembled the frozen revision-C bundle (sha256 798c00e0…, 23/23 SHA256SUMS), re-scored and re-bootstrapped the holdout, and checked each proposed paper edit against its original text and evidence. Everything replicates except one proposed Results sentence: 13, not 15, wrong cells carry a printed RM gold. Criteria 1–4 hold; criterion 5 needs correction.
notes: Verification was performed against pinned bytes, not prose. I reassembled the six revision-C base64 parts and obtained sha256 798c00e0e8e785b54018f43263459473a9bb6e3fafaaa3017233f23712d6ce05 with 23/23 payload files matching the internal SHA256SUMS; re-scored the 80-receipt holdout from holdout_per_receipt.json (P0 264/320=0.8250, P2 279/320=0.871875, delta +0.046875, whole-receipt 35/80→44/80); re-ran both bootstraps with random.Random(20260918), 10 000 draws (receipt [0.009375,0.084375]; company-cluster [-0.003425,0.089744]; 5th percentiles 0.015625 and 0.005747; P(delta<0.03)=0.1857 and 0.2392; dominant cluster removed +0.034615; 44 clusters with sizes 15,8,4,4,3,3,2×5,1×33; sum of squared weights 0.06125, 16.33 effective clusters); recomputed 16/5/23 cluster signs, 33 singletons, the 25-up/10-down sign test (p=0.01667), the whole-receipt delta +0.1125 with interval including zero, the six prompt lengths (519/1674/2602), the four P2 contamination strings, the four mislabelled smoke rows, the literal backslash-n template, the exhibit-pointer file counts (20 vs 23), and the stale manifest report row (86b64db9… vs e813ae25…). One defect found, which is why this returns for a synthesis-level correction rather than a fresh lens wave: the proposed Results/secondary replacement, mirrored in synthesis §6 item 2, states “15 are totals whose gold carries a printed RM token”, but error_audit.jsonl shows 15 wrong totals of which 13 carry RM gold (13 of the 15 agree modulo non-digits); the same paragraph’s third sentence implies 13, so the text is self-contradictory and would publish an overstated label-artifact count. findings.notes: Section 3 correctly separates completed, independently reviewed work from the in-flight wave.
